claims.statement: Collective-purchase rules are seller/admin-writable per-product configurations, but each created collective snapshots its rule so later configuration changes do not change the in-flight offer.
The collective-rule database trigger enforces real discounts, increasing quantity thresholds, decreasing prices, a maximum of four lots, and coherent targets, rather than trusting the seller form.

Joining a collective is serialized and revalidates status, deadline, product/store availability, aggregate stock, and participant caps; an existing participant may increase quantity after the cap while a new participant may not.

A collective becomes viable only when target quantity, minimum distinct participants, and the store minimum aggregate value are met; a viable collective closes only at its deadline, cap, final lot, or owner-forced close, while a nonviable expired collective creates no orders.

At collective closure, the database creates one pending PIX order per participant at the best reached lot, debits stock once, and allocates shared freight and rounding remainders so participant totals equal collective totals exactly.

Collective payment expiry is idempotent and, after the stamped payment deadline, cancels only pending orders and restores their stock; paid orders and prices remain intact and the collective remains closed.

The scheduled collective tick requires the Asaas webhook bearer token and service-role configuration, records observability, runs deterministic lifecycle evaluation and payment expiry, and uses an LLM only to author progress wording with a fixed-copy fallback.
Seller AI collective-rule suggestions are generated from product and sales context, deterministically validated and retried at most three times, and are not persisted until the seller submits a rule.
Future-sale checkout uses the future-sale entry’s reserved stock and optional price, and any cart containing a future-sale item is blocked unless the buyer has a nonblank CNPJ or IE profile.

Reverse auctions permit authenticated buyers to publish a future-ending request, restrict bids to active-store owners with one updatable bid per store, and restrict adjudication to the posting buyer and a bid belonging to that auction.
Adjudicating a reverse auction records the winning bid and audit event but does not create an automatic order; payment and delivery remain an arrangement between buyer and winning manufacturer.
Affiliate batch enrollment skips products that are already affiliated or no longer eligible and preserves the product-specific commission with a 5% fallback.

Checkout credits affiliate commission only for a nonblank referral identifier matching an approved affiliation applicable to the line product or store; it clears legacy automatic attribution first, so organic purchases receive no affiliate commission.

Affiliate PIX data has no generic write policy, is changed only through a dedicated validated and audited RPC, and requires administrative or service confirmation plus 24 hours before payout eligibility.

Collective creation and participation server actions require an authenticated user, validate their inputs with Zod, and apply a five-attempt-per-minute per-user rate limit before invoking the database RPCs.
A collective creator cannot supply a quantity that already reaches the target, and a collective configured for shared freight requires the creator to supply a delivery address.
The checkout application splits a multi-store cart into store-specific order requests, while the database checkout RPC enforces one store per resulting order.

Checkout reads the captured affiliate reference from its cookie and passes it through the six-argument checkout entrypoint; the overload chain retains the separate four-argument referral-attribution wrapper without a default referral argument.
